summary: Lata Chhatre specializes in philosophy, Indology, and Buddhist studies. She taught at Savitribai Phule Pune University, serving as Reader in the Department of Philosophy (attested 2009) and Visiting Faculty (attested 2026).

Lati Rinpoche (1922–2010) was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Ganden Shartse Monastery and Gyume Tantric College, served as Abbot of Ganden Shartse Monastery (~1976–1984), and held posts at Namgyal Monastery and the University of Virginia.

Latika Lahiri (b. 1923) is a scholar in Sinology and Buddhist studies. She studied at Peking University under supervisor Xianlin Ji from around 1958 to 1961 and later held a post at the University of Delhi.

Laura Harrington works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies. She studied at Columbia University under Ryuichi Abe, Theodore Riccardi, Gary A. Tubb, Lobsang Jamspal, Kirti Rinpoche, Nathaniel Dickson, and Gregory A. Hillis.

Lauran R. Hartley is a Tibetologist who held positions at Indiana University Bloomington, Rutgers University, and the Latse Contemporary Tibetan Cultural Library. As of 2026, she is Adjunct Assistant Professor and Modern Tibetan Studies Program Director at Columbia University.

Laurence Austine Waddell (1854–1938) worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies after earning a medical degree at the University of Glasgow. He served in the British and Indian military services, taught at Kolkata's Medical College, and was Professor of Tibetan at UCL (1906–1908).

Laurence Binyon (1869–1943) was a scholar in history, archaeology, Sinology, and Japanology. Educated at St Paul's School and Trinity College, Oxford, he worked at the British Museum (~1893–1933) and held a post at Harvard University (~1933–1934).

Laurie L. Patton (b. 1961) works in Indology and religious studies. Educated at Harvard and the University of Chicago (PhD), she held posts at Emory and Duke, served as President of Middlebury College (2015–2024), and became President of the AAAS (~2023).
Lavanya V. Eswar is a scholar in Indology and philosophy. Attested in 2026, she is a Ph.D. scholar at the Kuppuswami Sastri Research Institute studying under doctoral supervisor V. Yamuna Devi.

Lawrence E. Sullivan is a religious studies scholar. He served as Professor of the History of Religions at Harvard Divinity School, Director of the Center for the Study of World Religions (attested 2000–2004), and Professor of Theology at the University of Notre Dame.

Lawrence Heyworth Mills (1837–1918) was a scholar of Iranian and Central Asian studies and Indology. He studied at New York University and held a professorship at the University of Oxford (attested 1903).
Lawrence J. McCrea is a scholar of Indology and philosophy who studied under Sheldon Pollock. Attested in 2026, he serves as a Professor at Cornell University.

Lawrence William Nelson is a Buddhist studies scholar. He completed studies across several institutions, including Butler, Indiana, NYU, Northwestern, and St. John's College, ultimately earning a Doctor of Philosophy and Religion from the California Institute of Integral Studies.

LeRoy Carr Barret (1877–1960) was a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He studied at Washington and Lee University (~1894–1898) and completed his studies at Johns Hopkins University (~1899–1903) under Maurice Bloomfield.

Leah Zahler worked in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She earned her PhD from the University of Virginia, where she was supervised by Jeffrey Hopkins and also studied under Harvey B. Aronson, Geshe Wangyal, and Joe Bransford Wilson.

Lee Yearley is a scholar in religious studies, philosophy, and Sinology. He held a faculty career at Stanford University, serving as Professor (attested 1989–1992) and later as Emeritus (attested 2026).

Leedom Lefferts is a scholar in Buddhist studies and anthropology. Attested in 2011, he served as Professor of Anthropology, Emeritus at Drew University and Research Associate in the Department of Anthropology at the Smithsonian Institution.

Leela Aditi Wood specializes in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD from the University of Michigan (2005) under supervisors Luis O. Gómez and Martin J. Powers, and held a post at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute.

Leo Frobenius (1873–1938) was a German scholar in history and archaeology. He held posts at the Berlin Society for Anthropology, the Frobenius Institute (1920–1938), Goethe University Frankfurt (1932–1938), and the Museum der Weltkulturen (1935–1938).

Leo M. Pruden (1938–1991) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied under Taitetsu Unno and Akira Hirakawa, including at the University of Tokyo, and held posts at Brown University, the Nyingma Institute, and the University of Oriental Studies.
